identity: One continuous seated talking-head take, subject matted onto a designed near-monochrome canvas, with the SPEECH carried visually by kinetic typography: words fly in around the speaker at the instant they are spoken. Cut rhythm is irrelevant — typography choreography IS the rhythm. Sections are announced by giant accent-colored display words; brightness flips with the narrative (bright=solution, dark=problem); a music bed swells only at the CTA.

canvas.base: cream/paper texture with faint grid, near-monochrome
canvas.accent: one saturated color only (red here) — used for the hook disc, section display words, and key UI highlights
canvas.secondary_accents: at most 1-2 tinted words (blue product name, orange CTA keyword)

subject.treatment: background-removed (matted) with soft drop shadow, seated, centered or slightly off-center; a colored disc or shape may sit behind the subject in the hook
subject.scale: medium shot, whole torso visible — text needs the empty space around the head and shoulders
subject.narrative_lighting: bright canvas for hook/solution/features; DARK desk scene for the problem section — brightness follows the story, flipping exactly at narrative turns

typography.sync_rule: each word/phrase appears AT the moment it is spoken (word-level transcript timing), never as a bottom caption bar
typography.placement_rule: words compose AROUND the subject — beside the head, arcing over shoulders, stacked in clear space; never covering the face

scales.color: near-black on bright canvas / white on dark

scales.treatment: accent tint or heavier weight inside a kinetic phrase

typography.ui_mockups: when the speech describes product actions, animated UI props (pill buttons, dropdowns, toggles, sliders) appear and act out the words

sections.name: hook
sections.content: claim + tease, subject on accent disc, highest motion of the whole video (measured YDIF 16.9 vs 5.3 avg)

sections.name: problem
sections.content: DARK scene; the pain acted out visually (wall of broken text); ends at the pivot word ('but then I found ...')

sections.name: solution reveal
sections.content: flip back to bright; product named; one hero UI prop

sections.name: features x3
sections.content: numbered display-word sections, ~8-10s each, one capability acted out per section

sections.name: cta
sections.content: dark backdrop, platform logo, comment-keyword instruction; music swells (+21dB at 0.90 of runtime)

structure.motion_curve: front-loaded and decaying: measured per-section motion 16.9 → 9.5 → 5.8 → 4.3 → 4.2 → 2.0
structure.scene_changes: 5-6 background changes in 45s, at section boundaries only — every one marked by a whip/glitch/flash transition (measured flash clusters at 2.1, 7.9, 13.0, 31.2, 41.2s)

audio.role: music is a BED, not a driver — cuts do not lock to beats (40% within 100ms vs 28% random baseline)
audio.dynamics: flat and low under speech; single +21dB swell at the CTA
audio.speech: the voice is the lead audio throughout

rubric.words_visualized: every spoken phrase has a synced typographic event; target: >=90% of transcript words appear on screen within 150ms of utterance

expressible_today: per-phrase placed text with entrance animations (add_text at x/y)
text behind/around a matted subject (add_text_behind, personseg)
title cards / color screens for the CTA (add_title_card, add_color_screen)
gaps: typography CHOREOGRAPHY as a composed program: N per-phrase text groups with varied curves/arcs generated from the transcript in one pass (today: one add_text call per phrase, no arc/rotate paths)
subject matte onto a DESIGNED canvas (disc/texture behind a removed background) as a persistent look, not a per-frame effect
animated UI-mockup props (pills, toggles, dropdowns) as a graphics pack
narrative brightness flip as a scene-level design move the agent plans (needs the agent to map problem/solution spans from the transcript)
